How to read ✕

Actor

a user nameThe person signed in when the change was made. SystemA service did it: a shelf that expired, an activation verified. Not recorded by nameAn older Administration event that names its actor by user id; the id is in Record details.

Action

✓Loop activatedActivated, acknowledged, approved, verified. ◐Event shelvedShelved. ✕Loop deletedDeleted. Draft editedAny other change.

Filters

Entity, User and Event type ask the server, so they reach older records. Find searches only the rows fetched. User matches the exact user name.

Audit chain

Entries are hash-chained by audit-service. Verify audit chain asks the service to walk the chain and shows its answer.

State

◐Validated ◐Shadow evaluatedWaits for an independent approver. ◐ApprovedWaits for activation. ✕Activation failed ✕Partially acknowledgedNOT active: activate again once the fleet is fixed.

Rules

ApproveNeeds cpm.config.approve (by someone other than the author). ApprovalAn approval is bound to the content hash and expires. A self-approval, an expired approval or a stale hash is refused by the server. Site-wide changea site-wide or objective / test-permission change needs an approver with the ControlAuthority role (the server's rule, stated nowhere today: question 11)

Marks

✓The role holds the permission.—The role does not hold it.

When a permission change applies

Everyone with this role is signed out within a few seconds, and gets the new permissions when they sign in again.

Why versions are stored

Every stored window carries these versions in its payload, so any historical verdict can be attributed to the formula that produced it.
